_readme: External links that are NOT citations. A citation is evidence for a fact the page asserts and did not originate; it belongs in the page's Sources block. A RESOURCE link tells the reader where to go next — install this free font, sign in here to rename your account, file your proposal at this address — and belongs inline in the sentence that sends them, where it is useful. Both kinds still take their rel from data/source_authority.json; only the Sources-block obligation differs. Keyed by route, listing the domains that are resource links ON THAT PAGE: the same domain can be a citation on one page and a destination on another, which is exactly why this is scoped per page and not per domain. A page whose every external domain is listed here needs no Sources block. Same bar as data/library_hub_exclusions.json and every other ledger in this repo: entries are discussed decisions with a reason and a date, never added to make a page pass. If a link is really backing a claim, the fix is to write the Sources block, not to list it here.

_fields.domains: Domains on this page whose links are destinations, not evidence.
_fields.reason: What the reader is being sent to do.

answers/what-font-does-linkedin-use/inde.reason: "Install Source Sans 3 for free" — the specimen page is where the reader downloads the lookalike font, not evidence for what LinkedIn uses.

answers/what-font-does-pinterest-use/ind.reason: "Install Poppins for free" — a download destination. The Grilli Type link on the same page IS a citation and is in the Sources block.

The guide teaches the process rather than reporting a fact about it, so these are destinations. If it later asserts a dated fact about the process, that fact needs a Sources block of its own.
